author_or_org: Wei Zou, Mingwen Dong, Miguel Romero Calvo, Shuaichen Chang, Jiang Guo, Dongkyu Lee, Xing Niu, Xiaofei Ma, Yanjun Qi, Jiarong Jiang

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The paper introduces eTAMP, described as the first attack achieving cross-session, cross-site compromise without direct memory access.
claims.quote: We introduce Environment-injected Trajectory-based Agent Memory Poisoning (eTAMP), the first attack to achieve cross-session, cross-site compromise without requiring direct memory access.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: A single contaminated observation can silently poison an agent's memory and later activate on different websites, bypassing permission-based defenses.
claims.quote: A single contaminated observation (e.g., viewing a manipulated product page) silently poisons an agent's memory and activates during future tasks on different websites, bypassing permission-based defenses.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: eTAMP achieves attack success rates up to 32.5% on GPT-5-mini, 23.4% on GPT-5.2, and 19.5% on GPT-OSS-120B.
claims.quote: First, eTAMP achieves substantial attack success rates: up to 32.5% on GPT-5-mini, 23.4% on GPT-5.2, and 19.5% on GPT-OSS-120B.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The paper reports Frustration Exploitation: environmental stress can increase attack success rates by up to 8 times when agents struggle with dropped clicks or garbled text.
claims.quote: Second, we discover Frustration Exploitation: agents under environmental stress become dramatically more susceptible, with ASR increasing up to 8 times when agents struggle with dropped clicks or garbled text.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: More capable models are not necessarily more secure; GPT-5.2 shows substantial vulnerability despite superior task performance.
claims.quote: Notably, more capable models are not more secure. GPT-5.2 shows substantial vulnerability despite superior task performance.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Agent memory stores past interactions to personalize future tasks, creating a persistent attack surface spanning websites and sessions.
claims.quote: Memory makes LLM-based web agents personalized, powerful, yet exploitable. By storing past interactions to personalize future tasks, agents inadvertently create a persistent attack surface that spans websites and sessions.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The experiments in the paper were conducted on (Visual)WebArena.
claims.quote: Our experiments on (Visual)WebArena reveal two key findings.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The rise of AI browsers such as OpenClaw, ChatGPT Atlas, and Perplexity Comet is cited as underscoring the need for defenses against environment-injected memory poisoning.
claims.quote: With the rise of AI browsers like OpenClaw, ChatGPT Atlas, and Perplexity Comet, our findings underscore the urgent need for defenses against environment-injected memory poisoning.
